headline: CNG filling stations to close nationwide on July 30
summary: The Bangladesh CNG Filling Station and Conversion Workshop Owners Association has announced a one-day strike to demand a commission increase.
details: All CNG filling stations across Bangladesh will remain closed from 6 AM to 12 midnight on July 30. The decision was announced by the Bangladesh CNG Filling Station and Conversion Workshop Owners Association during a press conference in Dhaka.

The association is demanding that the current commission be increased to a minimum of 13.96 BDT per cubic meter. They warned that if their demands are not met, they will launch an indefinite nationwide strike starting August 23.
Owners stated that the current commission was fixed at 8 BDT per cubic meter on September 1, 2015. They argue that this rate is no longer sustainable due to extreme inflation over the last 11 years.

Other factors contributing to the crisis include the rise in minimum wages, the high cost of spare parts, and increased bank guarantees and lease fees. The association mentioned they will continue discussions with the government while pursuing their program.

headline_marked: Green chili prices [[surge past 200 taka per kg]] in Dhaka markets
headline: Green chili prices surge past 200 taka per kg in Dhaka markets
summary: Prices have nearly doubled in a month, with some markets seeing rates as high as 280 taka per kg due to heavy rains and floods.
details: Green chili prices in Dhaka have spiked, with high-quality chilies now selling for over 200 taka per kg. In some markets, prices have reached as high as 280 taka per kg, a significant jump from 100-120 taka just a month ago.

The price hike is primarily attributed to continuous heavy rainfall and recent floods, which reduced the supply of vegetables. Waterlogging in various farming areas has destroyed crops, preventing the supply from recovering.

Market surveys at Mohammadpur Krishi Market and Town Hall Market showed prices between 200 and 280 taka per kg. In Karwan Bazar, high-quality chilies are selling for 200 taka, while ordinary quality is around 160 taka.
Sellers report that almost all vegetables have seen price increases due to low wholesale supply and high demand. Only a few types of vegetables are currently available for under 100 taka per kg.
Additionally, onion prices have also risen by 5 taka per kg, now selling between 45 and 50 taka per kg, compared to 35-40 taka a week ago.
The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has forecast another five days of continuous rain, which may further impact vegetable supplies and market prices.
